Diplomatic Envoys and Royalty From Around the World Meet with His Majesty King Rama IX

After a couple days adjusting from jet lag the diplomats were treated to tours of the city, lavish dinners and plush accommodations before one evening an agenda was slipped under the doors of the diplomats that requested their presence in a conference room to begin the seminar.

Upon arriving at the room they were instead greeted by His Majesty King Rama IX dressed in a simple business suit, standing at the head of the table, his wheel chair off in the corner behind him. After greetings were exchanged and all were seated His Majesty began to speak in a soft conversational tone:

I hope you will all forgive me for cancelling the seminar on Royal Protocol, those formalities could only be counterproductive to this meeting. I hope that we can engage in discussion here as equals and more importantly as friends. When I invited diplomatic envoys I never expected such esteemed guests, it is truly an honor to host you here and I thank you for joining me today.

It is my wish that you enjoy your time here and I invite you to stay as long as you wish here in my home and experience all my country has to offer. As you’ve seen from the tours in the short time since I started my reign over this country I have made significant steps to improving the quality of life and stability. With my council I have endeavored and succeeded in improving the manufacturing and agricultural sectors, completed a new plan for education and begun several forward facing research projects.

However I have brought you all here today because there is something that I cannot accomplish alone, something that needs a more global approach. We have a refugee crisis in this country, six hundred thousand have crossed the border from Myanmar into Thailand in order to escape the civil war and slaughter that continues to persist within their nation. This conflict has continued for decades, since the time of their independence from the British Empire they have been plagued by numerous successive military coups that have left the country fractured and broken. Currently there are 16 warring factions within Myanmar, including those currently in power, the Tatmadaw. This region continues to slowly tear itself apart to this day. Generations have grown up there knowing nothing but conflict.

It is understandable that this conflict has gone for the most part unnoticed, our focus has been elsewhere and this conflict has remained isolated, but it has been allowed to simmer in the background for decades. This civil war has had many innocent victims, there is a plethora of evidence has mounted against the Tatmadaw, accusations included burning down entire villages, planting landmines, using civilians as slave labour, using civilians as minesweepers and recruiting children to fight as soldiers in their army.

More recently the nationwide ceasefire failed to gather support from half of the factions, and this should have been our call to action, we must face the reality that this conflict has no end in sight. My refugee camps are already overcrowded and the quality of life is poor, our resources are already stretched thin. I do not wish to re-locate these people elsewhere in the world, I wish to deal with the root of the problem, the Tatmadaw, and give these people a home to return to.

However it’s not enough to simply remove them from power, another military force will simply fill the void that is left and once again we will be in the same position we are today. The Burmese people wish for peace but have forgotten how to practice anything but war.

The situation is complex, the currently elected party, The National League for Democracy, is essentially held hostage and unable to make significant change, lest they incite a military coup. The elected government acts as a smoke screen, unable to touch or limit the power of the Tatmadaw while legitimizing their actions as the will of the people.

This is where I need to ask of you a great deal, and I do not expect an answer today, but I request you to bring my message home with you and consult with your heads of state and decide if this matter deserves action.

My council and I have developed a plan for the recovery and healing of Myanmar, I ask you to place your trust in me and join me to remove the Tatmadaw from power and install a Royal Thai Administration to provide oversight to the democratically elected parliament currently in place. However, it needs to start here, if we present a united front and show them the force and overwhelming odds they face, it is possible we may be able to coerce them into accepting our reforms. Without your support, action cannot and will not be taken, going forward alone would result in drawn out conflict and more loss of life.

I now encourage you to please voice any questions or concerns you may have.

His Majesty’s Royal Plan for Prosperity in Myanmar has several steps:

Initial Phase

  • International pressure to coerce the Tatmadaw into accepting sweeping reform

Phase 1 – 1st 6 months

  • Removal of Tatmadaw from positions of power within the government and military
  • Installation of Royal Thai Administration to provide oversight to the democratically elected parliament
  • Deployment of Royal Thai Army peacekeeping forces

Phase 2 – 6 Months – 5th year

  • Thai assets moved into Myanmar to provide support in education and healthcare
  • Restructuring of present Tatmadaw Forces into new Myanmar Civil Corps. Who will be unarmed and employed to work on infrastructure projects across the country to bring the nation into the modern age.
  • Re-integration of refugee and displaced individuals to rural regions
  • Introduction of initiatives to develop economy focusing on industry, agriculture and resource extraction
  • Gradual reallocation of budget from military spending to invest in healthcare, education, and social programs.

Phase 3 - 5 years onward

  • Retraction of Royal Thai Army Peacekeeping forces to military bases in favor of newly re-established national police forces
  • Wind down Civil Corps in favor of positions through outplacement initiatives to the private sector.

It's important to note that the Tatmadaw consumes a large portion of the annual budget in Myanmar and has a larger standing army than Thailand and newer military assets. Thailand would not pursue any action without international support.
